cases.title: Robust chamber command
analytic_checks: Affine disturbance dependence makes endpoints necessary and sufficient.
Policy stays inside actuator bounds and maps both state endpoints into C.
x=0 forces fixed u=0 while x=5 forces fixed u<=-9/10.
The one-step interval inclusion supports induction from x0 in C.
limitations: Exact current state, exact actuator, fixed affine model and bounded warming are assumed.

cases.title: Iteration deadline and floor
analytic_checks: Exact equality recurrence agrees with finite-geometric-sum formula through k=9.
Monotone bound brackets tolerance at neighboring integers.
Positive geometric remainder prevents reaching the floor in finite time.
limitations: Recurrence bounds errors; actual errors may be smaller. Runtime assumes stated fixed per-step costs.

cases.title: 0.B1 — Accept bounded-error readings
analytic_checks: Interval containment requires both endpoints; rejection leaves passing and failing possibilities.
limitations: Deterministic sensor bound is assumed.

cases.title: 0.B2 — Command before warming
analytic_checks: Endpoint containment checks the robust interval.
The alternative command is algebraically valid but requires observing w before choosing u.
limitations: The hardware information order is part of the problem.

cases.title: 0.B3 — Attainable error tolerance
analytic_checks: Equality recurrence witnesses failure of earlier universal budgets.
Strict versus non-strict tolerance distinguishes k=6 from k=7.
limitations: Guarantees come from the bound rather than observations of actual error.

cases.title: 0.B4 — Exact disturbance range
analytic_checks: At x=5 maximum cooling gives lower achievable endpoint 9/2+d, proving necessity.
Feedback actuator bound and monotone state/disturbance endpoints prove sufficiency.
Induction requires x0 in [0,5].
limitations: No disturbances or delays outside the stipulated model are covered.

cases.title: Balanced sensor reconstruction
analytic_checks: Exact Gram identity proves equal stretch in every direction.
Inverse image of the sensor box is a rotated square; convex squared length is bounded by its vertices.
limitations: Calibration is exact and only additive sensor errors are modeled.

cases.title: Nearly redundant sensor sensitivity
analytic_checks: Exact elimination produces the stated state error.
Positive eigenvalues satisfy the symmetric matrix characteristic polynomial and equal singular values.
Coincident rows at second coefficient=1 reduce rank.
limitations: This chosen perturbation illustrates sensitivity, not a statistical frequency.

cases.title: A.B1 — Assembly limit with reconstructed error
analytic_checks: Balanced inverse gives exact componentwise sensor-error bound; extremal same-sign sensor errors attain it.
limitations: The specification concerns the true displacement, not just the estimate.

cases.title: A.B2 — Minimum length and identification
analytic_checks: Polynomial coefficient identity gives all-solution norm and unique minimum.
Nonnegativity bounds t in [-3,3]; feasible counterexample disproves certification.
limitations: Minimum length is a stated convention, not additional sensor information.

cases.title: A.B3 — Scales and a normalized norm
analytic_checks: Cauchy–Schwarz gives a uniform bound; the constructed direction attains equality.
Separate-coordinate box enlarges the Euclidean ball, explaining the looser bound.
limitations: Chosen position and velocity scales define the assumed uncertainty geometry.

cases.title: A.B4 — Third-sensor least-squares audit
analytic_checks: Exact normal equations and both residual orthogonality equations hold.
Positive leading pivot and determinant establish positive-definite Gram matrix.
Pythagorean least-squares decomposition proves global minimality and uniqueness.
limitations: Equal residual weights are a modeling choice; the perturbation is particular, not worst-case.

cases.title: Weighted shared-flow allocation
analytic_checks: All four KKT conditions hold; positive Hessian ensures strict convexity.
For every feasible displacement, the exact cost difference is -lambda*sum(delta)+positive quadratic.
Active-set range follows from u>0 and lambda>0; value derivative is -lambda.
limitations: Weight four is a design choice. Flow is normalized by one litre per minute.

cases.title: Nonlinear endpoint clearance
analytic_checks: Exact quadratic inequality solves the full feasible interval.
Tracking objective decreases throughout [0,1], giving the right feasible endpoint.
Feasibility, nonnegative multiplier, complementary slackness and zero stationarity hold.
Constraint second derivative 1/5 and objective second derivative one prove convexity.
limitations: Static endpoint model over [0,1]; no continuous-trajectory guarantee or model error is assumed.

cases.title: B.B1 — Feasible transfer improvement
analytic_checks: Exact one-dimensional expansion has positive curvature and feasible minimizing transfer.
Gradient is orthogonal to the budget tangent and balanced by its normal.
limitations: The transfer comparison preserves the shared budget.

cases.title: B.B2 — Budget sensitivity
analytic_checks: Both candidate allocations satisfy every KKT condition within the same active-set range.
Exact quadratic value difference verifies first-order shadow-price remainder.
limitations: Large budget changes may cross active-set boundaries.

cases.title: B.B3 — Feasibility repair
analytic_checks: Projection correction is parallel to line normal (1,1), preserving nearest-point optimality.
All primal constraints hold after repair.
Exact quadratic difference gives the cost gap; original point is infeasible.
limitations: A repaired feasible point may remain suboptimal; requirements define acceptable feasibility tolerance.

cases.title: B.B4 — Robust nonlinear clearance
analytic_checks: Affine disturbance dependence selects w=-0.03 as the exact worst case.
Monotonic clearance and objective identify the unique robust boundary optimum.
All KKT conditions hold for the convex robust inequality.
At a=0 clearance is maximal, proving exact general feasibility threshold d<=0.2.
limitations: Bounded error model assumes the true clearance is enclosed for all commands under consideration.
All real-world settings are constructed teaching models with stated units and assumptions.
Checks verify mathematical calculations and analytic conditions, not physical model validity.
